title: Hawkins, Carter, Buster Bailey and trouble with blues and ballads
summary: Roy cites Coleman Hawkins, Benny Carter and Buster Bailey as models and says he could not play blues or ballads then.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Had you become a Coleman Hawkins and Benny Carter fan by then?
Oh, that was before then! I told you, I got my first job playing Coleman Hawkins' chorus! Then after that, I was Benny Carter, you know -- him and Coleman. Then Buster Bailey.
What did you like about him? Speed?

Yeah. He could get over his horn, man, and I dug that, you know. The things he played. I mean, he didn't just get over. You know, I heard some records last night that they were playing on (?), it was Clark Terry and the boy that died...the trumpet player that died...

Yeah. And it was ridiculous, man. They was playing all that fast, and the things they were playing, they were just trying to figure out something fast to play, and every once in a while they'd have to stop and hold a note and...heh-heh... Of course, that was a long time ago, but hell, it still was that same thing about playing that fast, you know. Because I tried to keep the string going, you know, but not with the same thing or repeating the same thing. And I couldn't play no blues.
There wasn't any blues in the shows that you worked on?
Sure. There would be the singers.
But you couldn't get with that?
Well, I never... You know, you never even think about it, really... I think your light is starting to do some strange things...

So that's the way that works out, you know. I don't know... The Blues is something that was just... I didn't like ballads either then! And I think the reason I didn't like them was I couldn't play them. I'll be honest with you, you know. I hear a lot of cats now, they're playing ballads and they have to triple it up, you know. Playing in the meter is a little harder than being... You know, playing fast, all you got to do is spend a little time and rehearse, just rehearse, what are you going to riff, you're going to set 'em up and just back 'em up, right? But when you're playing the ballad and playing in the meter, man, you got to have some feeling, you got to have some kind of sound that's going to make some sense, you know what I mean... You move just like a singer would. You know? And that ain't easy. Boy, when I was with Horace Henderson, man, I used to get so mad when they'd play something slow. I'd want to walk off the bandstand.
When did you go with Horace? Was that after you came off the road with...?
One of those times. I think I went with Horace in '28 or something like that.
